messages:
incident-bot: 🔥 INCIDENT CREATED INC-2024-ACME-42 — Dedicated pool 'pool-acme-eu-2' for customer 'Aurelia Systems' is at 99% GPU utilization. Queue depth growing; requests are STARTING to queue >30s. Severity: HIGH. Paging oncall.

sara.ng: I'm on it. paging @jon.k for backup. first look: metrics show a sudden sustained increase in tokens/sec from that tenant ~T-35m. no host-level OOMs.

jon.k: joining. thanks. can you dump the pool allocation and tenant share?

sara.ng: running: `redwoodctl pool describe pool-acme-eu-2 --json` and `redwoodctl allocations list --pool pool-acme-eu-2 | grep aurelia`

sara.ng: output snippet: ```
pool: pool-acme-eu-2
GPUs: 12 (A100s)
current_allocations:
  aurelia-tenant: 0.82 (82% of pool)
  shared-burst: 0.10
  other-tenants: 0.08
queueing: avg 32s latency
```

maya.p: egal here. customer is on Dedicated (reserved) tier — they own most of the pool, looks like their workload spiked. any quick levers?

jon.k: two immediate options: 1) allow temporary burst to shared capacity (violates isolation but reduces customer error rate), 2) throttle the tenant (reduce concurrency / per-key qps), 3) spin ephemeral burst nodes via autoscale if pool was configured with burst capacity. what's the config?

sara.ng: checking pool policy: `burst.enabled=false`, `reserved=true`, `autoscale.max_extra=0` — customer opted out of burst during deployment.

ravi.cs: CS note: Aurelia's slack is already pinging their SREs, they report degraded user-facing features (~10% of requests failing). They're asking for ETA and whether we can add capacity.

lee.englead: we need to preserve SLA and contractual isolation. short-term we can enable a controlled burst as an exception while we sort commit. Ops, can we enable burst for this pool for up to 30m and cap it to X GPUs?

ops-bot: runbook check: enabling burst for a reserved pool requires exec approval and a ticket. Command: `redwoodctl pool burst enable --pool pool-acme-eu-2 --gpus 4 --duration 1800 --reason "emergency customer mitigation"`

jon.k: i'll take the risk call with oncall authority. propose: enable burst + limit to 4 GPUs, gate traffic with rate limits to avoid unlimited spike, notify customer. If we see cost blowout we roll back.

maya.p: +1 for controlled burst. also start throttling concurrency to reduce queueing while burst spins up: `redwoodctl tenant update aurelia-tenant --max-concurrency 40` (current 100).

sara.ng: doing throttling now. `Applied max-concurrency=40` — monitoring.

ops-bot: burst enable command executed by jon.k at T+12m: `--gpus 4 --duration 1800`. New pool capacity 16 GPUs.

incident-bot: UPDATE INC-2024-ACME-42 — Burst enabled (4 GPUs). Observed GPU util across pool dropping to 74% within 70s. Queue depth reduced to avg 8s.

ravi.cs: communicated to customer: "We've enabled a temporary capacity increase and throttled concurrency to stabilize traffic. We're continuing to investigate root cause and will follow up in 1h." They acknowledged.

lee.englead: good. follow-up: create a post-incident action item to offer Aurelia a Dedicated scale-up or commit increase, since they consistently hit 80%+ during peak. Also check whether their workload pattern can be batched or quantized to reduce usage.

jon.k: digging into request patterns — looks like one job in their system started wide fanout at T-40m. Potentially a bad retry loop. I've opened a wiretap on tenant traffic: `redwoodctl flows tail --tenant aurelia-tenant --filter "prompt_length>2000"`

sara.ng: found a noisy service hitting many long-context calls. flagged to customer SRE to patch.

maya.p: I'll start the mitigation doc and postmortem skeleton: root-cause hypothesis, timeline, mitigations, follow-ups (quota change, burst policy review, autoscale enablement option).

ops-bot: reminder: we must record authorization for burst exception in ticket INC-2024-ACME-42-authorizations.

jon.k: starting to scale down burst early at T+45m since traffic back to normal levels. executing: `redwoodctl pool burst disable --pool pool-acme-eu-2`

incident-bot: RESOLUTION NOTE: Burst disabled, pool returned to reserved capacity. Final GPU utilization stabilized at avg 32%. Customer reports degradation resolved.

pm-amy: action items for PM/CS: discuss offering a buffer (2-4 GPU reserved burst) as an add-on for Aurelia, and coordinate committed upgrades.

ravi.cs: I'll set up a customer follow-up for tomorrow with the SRE and account team.

lee.englead: postmortem owners: jon.k (technical), maya.p (timeline/mitigation), sara.ng (onsite triage), ravi.cs (customer comms). Please ensure RCA draft by EOD tomorrow.

sara.ng: ack. closing thread after RCA created. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
